entries.content: up; (a-21) The word means 'receiving,' but with the prefix (ana) 'up,' as here, it has the active sense of 'taking up.' It is so translated except in 1Tim. 3.16. The more passive reception is seen in Acts 3.21, where another word is used.
with (b-12) En. see Note c, Matt. 3.11.
authority; (c-23) Exousia; a right one possesses. 'power' is dunamis, see Note, Matt. 10.1.
power, (c-5) Exousia; a right one possesses. 'power' is dunamis, see Note, Matt. 10.1. earth. (d-34) Or 'land.' see ch. 13.47 and Note, Matt. 5.5.
sight. (e-21) Lit. 'received up from their eyes.'

up (a-20) The word means 'receiving,' but with the prefix (ana) 'up,' as here, it has the active sense of 'taking up.' It is so translated except in 1Tim. 3.16. The more passive reception is seen in Acts 3.21, where another word is used.
(g-1) Lit. 'men brethren.' This is a Hebraism, and means no more than 'brethren.'
got (a-5) The Greek root is used for 'having' by whatever means. see Matt. 10.9; Luke 18.12; and Note, Luke 21.19.
Psalms, (b-9) See Ps. 69.25. and, (c-23) See Ps. 109.8.
accomplishing, (f-9) It was come and running its course of fulfilment as a feast.
blowing, (g-15) It is not 'wind,' but they heard blowing, as of hard breathing, for which the Greek is used. 'Blast' is too sudden and passing.

spread, (h-7) Or 'this voice having taken place ' but I believe what is in the text to be the sense. It was what happened at the place which brought the crowd there. it was not the mighty rushing wind being heard everywhere. The end of the verse goes to confirm this. What struck those who came was hearing their own tongues. Gen. 45.16 and Jer. 50.46 are examples. The rumours of Jacob's coming spread to Pharaoh's house.
appearing (b-18) Though used for 'illustrious,' 'glorious,' the Greek word has in it the sense of 'manifestation, appearing, displaying itself.' see Titus 2.11,13. Lord (c-22) 'Jehovah;' so ver 39.

Israel, (d-3) Lit. 'Men, Israelites,' as elsewhere, cf. ch. 1.16. to (e-14) 'Borne witness to, to you,' is not agreeable English; but 'approved,' in the modern use at any rate, is not the sense, and 'among you is feeble. The manifestation or demonstration was to the Jews. The witness was borne to them objectively, to Jesus as its subject.

hades, (h-9) 'in' (eis) hades. see Note, Matt. 11.23. gracious (i-15) Or 'holy,' hosios. It corresponds to the Hebrew chasid = merciful, gracious. see Note f, ch. 13.34,35; 2Chron. 6.42; and Heb. 7.26.
hades (h-19) 'in' (eis) hades. see Note, Matt. 11.23. Christ, (l-11) Or, 'of Christ. '
accepted (b-5) It means, 'to receive in full,' or 'with satisfaction;' or, as to an opinion or teaching, 'to accept and receive it as true.' see Note, Luke 8.40.

assembly] (e-16) See Note g, ch. 3.1. saved. (f-23) The remnant of Israel whom God was sparing. The Lord now added these to the Christian assembly. The present participle as here gives the character instead of the fact; as I might say, 'the being spared ones;' it is the class of persons God was then saving. It is not a doubt as to their being saved, nor a state, but a class. see Luke 13.23.

temple (d-10) Hieron, the general buildings. together (g-7) Some omit 'to the assembly,' ch. 2.47, and link 'together' with the end of ch. 2. Probably we should read 'the Lord added together daily such as should be saved. And Peter (or, 'Now Peter') and John went up into the temple.'

originator (a-3) This word is difficult to render in English. It is a 'leader,' but it is more. It is used for one who begins and sets a matter on. The Greek word occurs four times in the New Testament, here and ch. 5.31; Heb. 2.10; 12.2. In Heb. 12.2 it means, 'he began and finished the whole course;' 'the origin' or 'originator,' though the word is harsh in connexion with life. The word is only used of our Lord.
began. (c-29) 'Since time began' refers to 'holy prophets.' lit. 'his holy since-time-began prophets.'
Jesus (b-13) Lit. 'in Jesus.' En. see Matt. 3.11. among (c-17) This is a little more emphatic than usual. 'the resurrection which is from among [the] dead.'
stone. (d-20) Lit. 'head of corner,' see Ps. 118.22.
were (e-26) Or 'had been.' The council recognized them as former companions of Christ.

Lord, (a-17) Lit. 'despot,' 'the master' of a slave; 'one having sovereign power,' as Luke 2.29, 1Tim. 6.1,2, 2Tim. 2.21, Tit. 2.9; 1Pet. 2.18; 2Pet. 2.1; Jude 4; Rev. 6.10. God (b-21) Or 'thou art God,' i.e. Elohim, the One who is God.
cross. (d-18) Lit. 'on wood.' used for stocks, cross, and such ignominious and forcible means of punishment.
Him (e-1) Lit. 'this [one].' leader (f-10) See Note, ch. 3.15.
right (c-17) I apprehend that 'right,' 'proper,' is the sense; not merely that it did not please the apostles. 'Pleasing to God,' I understand, but used for man it is arbitrary.
freedmen, (e-13) Some translate 'Libertines,' referring it to Libertum, a city in Africa.
with (a-13) Or 'by' the Holy Spirit, but seen as in Stephen, that by which he spoke. 'which' refers grammatically to Spirit, but in sense to wisdom and Spirit both.
thus. (c-4) See Gen. 15.13-16. them (d-19) Lit. 'it,' the seed.
promised (g-12) The Greek means 'openly saying you will give,' Matt. 14.7. But we have no suited word but 'promise.' It is not the same word as in 'the time of promise.'
exceedingly (a-9) Lit. 'fair to God,' a known Hebraism.
brethren, (b-22) Lit. 'ye are men, brethren,' see Note at ch. 1.16.
[the] (c-22) The sentence is without the article and therefore much more emphatic. 'Lord' is a solemn title. The expression amounts to 'there came an utterance of Jehovah.'
it; (e-30) It has the sense of 'taking to or for oneself,' not merely deliverance as by removing the scourge, but by taking the people.
Yea (b-1) Quoted from the LXX. 'Yea' here has the force of 'Nay, but.'
High (d-4) See Luke 1.32. prophet, (e-15) See Isa. 66.1,2.
who (f-1) 'Who are such as.' ordained (g-7) See Gal. 3.19.

praying, (h-5) Lit. 'invoking,' 'calling on,' but in English we must have a word after this, which mars the connexion here. The Authorized Version seems to separate God and the Lord Jesus. 'Calling on the Lord' would leave out God. The Spirit of God, I doubt not, has purposely left out both 'Lord' and 'God'. No one can be called upon really but God, so that the word has great force as used here. I have said 'praying' for want of a better word.
(c-0) Ver. 37 in the Authorized Version is recognized as not genuine.
way, (e-21) * The Christian way. see Mark 10.32,52; Acts 19.9,23; 22.4; 24.14,22.
shone (f-19) The word is used for a very brilliant apparition. see Luke 17.24, 'lightens;' 24.4, 'shining.' It is the same Greek root as 'lightning.'

voice (g-9) Phone, accusative; in ver. 7 genitive; in ch. 22.9,14 accusative; in ch. 22.7 genitive. The genitive is 'to listen to,' or when the voice of a rumour reaches. It is the fact or physical hearing. The accusative is that the thing heard is before the mind.
persecutest. (h-16) The rest of ver. 5 and part of ver. 6, as in the A.V., is not found in the best manuscripts.
assemblies (a-2) Or 'assembly,' as many MSS. Spirit. (b-34) Or 'enjoyed peace ... and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, were multiplied.'
who (a-11) 'Who also.' They did not merely witness the effect of power, but their seeing it acted on them.

on (c-13) Epi. this goes on to the idea of confidence. I rest my faith on him, yet with the more general idea of looking to him with confidence. As in chs. 11.17; 16.31; 22.19; Rom. 4.5,24. see 2Tim. 1.12.
beholds (d-3) Theoreo, 'view with attention,' as John 6.40.
preaching (c-11) Lit. 'evangelizing.' In ver. 37 John 'heralded.' things,) (d-21) Or 'of all,' Gentile and Jew.
words (c-7) Rhema, see Note to John 17.14. word. (d-19) Logos, as ver. 36. See Note to John 17.14.
attendant. (a-24) Huperetes, as Luke 1.2, see Note, 1Cor. 4.1.

about (e-17) Where the computation begins is not stated. The judges were given after the land's being given by lot, and that order of things reached up to Samuel, to four hundred and fifty years, whenever that four hundred and fifty years began. It might be at the Exodus, and very probably so. But it is not that there were judges during all that time. Indeed, they were only raised up occasionally. I have no difficulty myself as to the chronology, notwithstanding the dicta of some. The main blunder of their computations lies in this. they have taken Eli and Samson as distinct periods from the Philistine oppression, whereas it is perfectly clear the Philistine oppression included both. We have to go on to Mizpeh for the close.

thus. (e-18) See Isa. 55.3. mercies (f-26) 'Mercies' and 'gracious one' (Hosios) are the same word, only singular and plural. It may, and sometimes does, mean 'holy,' but is not the regular word for it, which is Hagios. here it answers to chasid in Hebrew, which is contrasted in Ps. 89.19 with 'holy' (kadosh), which is applied to Jehovah (ver. 18). The beginning of the psalm speaks of the mercies (chasadim) or gracious ways of the Lord, and then in ver. 19 of that One in whom these graces or mercies are centred and conveyed, the Christ, to whom the apostle here applies it. The word chesed is generally 'grace' and 'loving-kindness' in God; chasid, 'pious,' 'gracious' applied to men, and 'merciful,' 'holy' to God. see Heb. 7.26.

one (f-13) 'Mercies' and 'gracious one' (Hosios) are the same word, only singular and plural. It may, and sometimes does, mean 'holy,' but is not the regular word for it, which is Hagios. here it answers to chasid in Hebrew, which is contrasted in Ps. 89.19 with 'holy' (kadosh), which is applied to Jehovah (ver. 18). The beginning of the psalm speaks of the mercies (chasadim) or gracious ways of the Lord, and then in ver. 19 of that One in whom these graces or mercies are centred and conveyed, the Christ, to whom the apostle here applies it. The word chesed is generally 'grace' and 'loving-kindness' in God; chasid, 'pious,' 'gracious' applied to men, and 'merciful,' 'holy' to God. see Heb. 7.26. another, (g-6) See Ps. 16.10.
God, (h-14) Or 'having served his own generation by the will of God.'

worshipping (a-17) The word translated 'worshipping,' 'worshippers,' and 'worshipped' at verses 43 and 50, also at chs. 16.14; 17.4 and 17, and 18.7, signified a numerous class of Gentiles who, acknowledging the vanity of idolatry and detesting its disorders, attended the Jewish worship.

worshippers, (a-13) The word translated 'worshipping,' 'worshippers,' and 'worshipped' at verses 43 and 50, also at chs. 16.14; 17.4 and 17, and 18.7, signified a numerous class of Gentiles who, acknowledging the vanity of idolatry and detesting its disorders, attended the Jewish worship.
was (c-7) 'Who was' is equivalent to 'which was,' referring to the temple of Jupiter.
received (a-8) 'Received gladly,' or 'with welcome.' see Luke 8.40.
putting (d-8) The infinitive, equivalent to 'in putting.' It is explanatory of what precedes.
Brethren, (a-11) Lit. 'Men brethren.' as ch. 1.16, so ver. 13.
blood. (f-22) Or 'and of fornication, and of what is strangled, and of blood.'
brethren, (g-14) Probably 'The apostles and the elder brethren to,' &c.

judgment, (h-11) Or, perhaps, 'assembled with one accord.' I have said 'having arrived at a common judgment' to give the sense of the Greek. 'Having come to one accord' would look like previous disunion. The fact of having arrived at one mind is here stated.
(a-0) Ver. 34 A.V. is not in the best MSS.
decrees (b-14) Or 'delivered to them the decrees to keep.'

through (c-4) forbidden (c-12) These participles have a causative force, especially thus disunited. 'Such being the case, they attempted to go.' country, (d-9) 'Phrygia and Galatia' are thrown into one by the one article.
down (c-3) These participles have a causative force, especially thus disunited. 'Such being the case, they attempted to go.'
colony. (e-16) Where the citizens had equal rights with those at the capital -- Rome.
gone, (b-12) Or 'gone out,' referring to the spirit.
praetors, (c-8) The magistrates of colonies. so vers. 36,38. too
praetors, (c-11) The magistrates of colonies. so vers. 36,38. too (d-6) Or 'with [them]' -- that is, with her masters.
praetors (a-7) The magistrates of colonies. so vers. 36, 38. lictors, (b-10) Attendants on the praetors.
believed, (d-5) * Lit. 'were convinced' or 'persuaded,' as Luke 16.31. worshipped, (e-18) See Note, ch. 13.43.
politarchs, (f-13) The special title of the city magistrates of Thessalonica.
politarchs (f-8) The special title of the city magistrates of Thessalonica.
as (h-11) The use of 'as' here is not of semblance of anything, but of purpose or intention.

Areopagus, (b-11) i.e. 'the hill of Mars.' The tribunal which watched over the morals of the Athenians, and saw that due honour was paid to the gods, held its sessions on Areopagus and was so designated. The word here may therefore refer either to the place, or to the tribunal which met there.

Areopagus (b-8) i.e. 'the hill of Mars.' The tribunal which watched over the morals of the Athenians, and saw that due honour was paid to the gods, held its sessions on Areopagus and was so designated. The word here may therefore refer either to the place, or to the tribunal which met there. Athenians, (c-10) Lit. 'Men Athenians.' The introduction of 'men' in these passages is not merely a Hebraism. It is the accustomed oratorical address in Greek. worship; (d-21) Or 'worship of the gods.'
of (a-16) Or 'earnestly occupied with.' The Greek word is the same as 'constrains,' 2Cor. 5.14. Christ. (b-27) Lit. 'the Christ Jesus;' i.e. the Christ was really come, and that Jesus was he.'
pure; (c-25) Or 'I, pure [from it] from henceforth, will go to the nations.'
Asiarchs (d-5) Honorary magistrates, of the principal persons of the province, specially charged with the public festivals.
Artemis (c-28) Latin, 'Diana.' Ephesians, (e-9) Lit. 'says, men Ephesians.' heaven? (f-39) Or 'from Jupiter.'
Derbe, (b-26) Or 'Gaius of Derbe and Timotheus.'
overpowered (c-12) In the act of being so. overpowered (d-25) 'Having been already overpowered.'
spoken (f-15) Or 'conversed.' as ch. 24.26, 'communed.' Luke 24.14,15; not as 'discoursed,' ver. 9.

purchased (b-29) Middle voice; reflexive. see Note e, Heb. 1.3. own. (c-35) I am fully satisfied that this is the right translation of ver. 28. To make it a question of the divinity of Christ (which I hold to be of the foundation of Christianity) is absurd. It has been questioned whether 'of his own' can be used thus absolutely in the singular. But we have it in John 15.19, and in the neuter singular for material things, Acts 4.32. The torturing of the passage by copyists arose, I believe, from not seeing, the real sense of it; a touching expression of the love of God.
away (f-5) An expression of effort. 'torn ourselves away' may be too strong, but it implies force.
out (a-4) Lit. 'diligently searched out,' as Luke 2.16. who (b-12) Who indeed.
whom (c-23) Or 'to bring us to a certain Mnason, a Cyprian, an old disciple with whom.'
pass, (a-5) Lit. 'it came to pass to me.' so ver. 17.
angel (c-35) The rest of ver. 9 A.V. is not in the best MSS.
(a-1) The speech is elliptical. finding him so, they would have judged him. world, (b-16) Lit. 'habitable world,' as Rev. 12.9.
man, (a-20) Or 'if there be anything amiss in the man.'
knowest. (b-31) Or 'thou knowest better than that;' that is, than to say, 'wilt thou go up to Jerusalem and be judged?'
done (c-5) Lit. 'I do.' The present tense and characteristic. see Note h, Gal. 2.14.
south-east. (a-33) Lit. 'looking down the south-west (wind) and down the north-west.' Down the wind is the point to which it blows.
frapping (b-8) Cables round the hull. Syrtis (c-18) * The dreaded quicksands of N. Africa.
saving (a-6) 'Save out of and through' a danger. see 1Pet. 3.20.
barbarians (c-3) * A name applied to all nations not of Greek or Roman descent and speaking a foreign language.
saved (a-25) 'Save out of and through' a danger. see 1Pet. 3.20. Nemesis (d-30) Lit. 'justice.'
however, (e-2) Or 'much rather.' 'however' is weak, but is I believe the best word.
man (a-15) 'The chief man' was an official title. Protos Melitaion. As an individual he was not, for his father was alive.
Forum (b-17) Market of Appius. Tabernae, (c-20) Three Taverns.
prefect, (d-16) The commanding officer of the Emperor's bodyguard
of (a-5) 'Assented to them as true.' It is used of giving credit to a person so as to follow him. as in ch. 5.36, 'obeyed.'
salvation (c-9) Rather 'that which saves' than salvation itself. see Luke 2.30; 3.6; Eph. 6.17.
